text: In the unique socio-cultural landscape of contemporary China, there is an ongoing scholarly debate regarding whether traditional demandingness or modern responsiveness—reflected as family closeness—is more conducive to fostering social–emotional skills. This study explores the relationship between closeness to families and empathy among students, specifically focusing on the mediating roles of emotional state, tolerance, and closeness to others.
source_label: Examining how emotional state, tolerance and closeness to others mediate the relationship between closeness to families and empathy in Chinese students
